note: Raw extracted items from TEA's 2023 Redesign Grade 8 Science Practice Assessment. correctAnswerReasoning is MY OWN derivation (no matching official key exists for this specific document - see 01-source-note.json answerKeyCaveat). Steps 2-3 subagent must independently verify each correctAnswerLetter against the option text/explanation before rewriting, not just copy it blindly.

items.prompt: Which statement about the sun is true?

options.A: It is the hottest star in the universe.
options.B: It is closer to Earth than any other star.
options.C: It is located in the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
options.D: It is the largest type of star known to exist.

items.reasoning: The Sun is not the hottest, largest, or centrally located star - it is simply the nearest star to Earth.

items.prompt: Which statement BEST describes a component of cell theory?

options.A: All cells form from molecules.
options.B: All cells come from preexisting cells.
options.C: All cells create genetically identical cells.
options.D: All cells reproduce from simpler cells.

items.reasoning: Core cell theory tenet: all cells arise from preexisting cells (cell division), not from molecules or 'simpler cells'.

items.prompt: Students measure a sample: Mass 35 g, Volume 14 cm3. Densities: Plywood 0.54, Aluminum 2.7, Rubber 1.1, Glass 2.5 (g/cm3). Based on the density of the sample, which material is the sample MOST LIKELY made of?

options.A: Plywood
options.B: Aluminum
options.C: Rubber
options.D: Glass

items.reasoning: 35/14 = 2.5 g/cm3, matches Glass exactly.

items.prompt: Controlled burns rid forests of tree limbs, dead leaves, and other debris. Which prediction can be made about a forest after a controlled burn has occurred?

options.A: The ability of plants to reproduce will decrease.
options.B: Important nutrients for new plant growth will be returned to the soil.
options.C: Short-term air quality in the area will improve.
options.D: Long-term biodiversity will be reduced.

items.reasoning: Burned organic debris returns nutrients (ash) to soil, a well-known ecological benefit of controlled burns.

items.prompt: Students bake a cake. Which statement BEST explains why baking a cake is evidence of a chemical reaction?

options.A: The state of matter of some of the ingredients changed while being cooked.
options.B: The total mass of the ingredients was the same before and after they were cooked.
options.C: The temperature of the ingredients increased as they absorbed thermal energy from the oven.
options.D: The ingredients formed a new substance after they were cooked in the oven.

items.reasoning: Formation of a new substance is the defining evidence of a chemical change; the other options describe physical changes or conservation of mass (true but not evidence of a chemical reaction specifically).

items.prompt: Which factor contributes MOST to the formation of a hurricane?

options.A: High water temperatures
options.B: High water density
options.C: High water oxygen levels
options.D: High water volume

items.reasoning: Hurricanes form over warm ocean water; warm water temperature drives the evaporation/convection that fuels the storm.

items.prompt: Which quantity determines the identity of an atom?

options.A: The number of neutrons
options.B: The number of protons
options.C: The number of electrons
options.D: The number of valence electrons

items.reasoning: Atomic number (number of protons) defines which element an atom is.

items.prompt: A balanced chemical equation is shown: 2Fe + 6HC2H3O2 -> 2Fe(C2H3O2)3 + 3H2. How many different elements are in the chemical equation?
items.reasoning: Elements present: Fe, H, C, O = 4 distinct elements (13 would be counting total atoms, not elements).

items.prompt: A student is looking at a model of a neutral atom. The model shows that the atom has 19 subatomic particles in the nucleus. Ten of those subatomic particles do not have a charge. Which statement about the model of the atom is true?

options.A: It has an atomic number of 19.
options.B: It has 10 electrons.
options.C: It has 9 protons.
options.D: It has an atomic mass of 29 amu.

items.reasoning: 19 nucleus particles total, 10 neutral (neutrons), so protons = 19-10 = 9. Atomic number = protons = 9, not 19. Neutral atom electrons = protons = 9, not 10. Mass number = protons+neutrons = 19, not 29.

items.prompt: Student 1 claims color change always means chemical change. Student 2 claims food coloring can change color without a chemical change. Red food coloring is added to water; it turns pink; a test shows the pink solution contains both water molecules and food-coloring molecules, unchanged. Based on these findings, which student is correct?

options.A: Student 1, because the food-coloring molecules were found in the pink solution
options.B: Student 1, because the state of matter changed when the food coloring was added
options.C: Student 2, because no new substance was formed when there was a color change
options.D: Student 2, because the red food coloring caused the water to change to a pink color

items.reasoning: Since the original molecules (water and food coloring) were both still present unchanged, no new substance formed - this is a physical change (mixing), supporting Student 2's claim, and specifically because no new substance formed (not merely 'D' which restates the color change without the key reasoning).

items.prompt: [REWRITE TARGET - originally open-response] Two students push on opposite sides of a crate on a frictionless surface: one pushes 40 N one direction, the other pushes 53 N the opposite direction. Which statement correctly describes the crate's motion?

options.A: The crate does not move because the forces are balanced.
options.B: The crate moves toward the side pushing with 53 N, with a net force of 13 N.
options.C: The crate moves toward the side pushing with 40 N, with a net force of 13 N.
options.D: The crate moves toward the side pushing with 53 N, with a net force of 93 N.

items.reasoning: Net force = 53-40 = 13N, in the direction of the larger force (53N side). Originally an open-response item in the source; converted to multiple-choice here per pipeline's rewrite step, since it has a single unambiguous fixed answer (13N toward the 53N side).

items.prompt: Overfishing table: 1979: 13%, 1989: 27%, 2008: 33% of fish species overfished. Which action would MOST LIKELY reverse this trend?

options.A: Increasing the total weight of fish that each ship can remove from the ocean each day
options.B: Requiring ships to return non-adult fish to the ocean so that they can grow and reproduce
options.C: Decreasing the number of policing ships in order to lessen capacity restrictions and regulations
options.D: Promoting meals centered around specific fish species in restaurants in order to increase profits

items.reasoning: Returning juvenile fish lets populations reproduce and recover; the other options would worsen overfishing.

items.prompt: A tennis ball is dropped down a stairwell. Which statement BEST describes the energy of the tennis ball?

options.A: The tennis ball's kinetic energy decreases as it falls to the ground.
options.B: The tennis ball has the most potential energy just before it is dropped.
options.C: The tennis ball has the most kinetic energy as soon as it is dropped.
options.D: The tennis ball's potential energy increases as it falls to the ground.

items.reasoning: Potential energy is greatest at maximum height (just before drop) and converts to kinetic energy as it falls; kinetic energy increases (not decreases) during the fall and is zero (not maximum) right when dropped.

items.prompt: The Olympic Mountains formed along the west coast of the United States at the boundary between the Juan de Fuca Plate and the North American Plate. Which type of boundary MOST LIKELY exists between these plates?

options.A: Convergent boundary, where the plates are moving toward each other
options.B: Convergent boundary, where the plates are moving parallel to each other
options.C: Transform boundary, where the plates are moving closer to each other
options.D: Transform boundary, where the plates are sliding past each other

items.reasoning: The Juan de Fuca Plate subducts beneath the North American Plate at the Cascadia subduction zone - a convergent boundary where plates move toward each other, which built the Olympic Mountains via accretion. Note options B and C are internally contradictory/nonsensical (convergent=parallel, transform=closer) and are effectively distractors by construction, not just difficulty - flagging for reviewer awareness.

items.prompt: A player hits a baseball with a baseball bat. Part A: Which statement about the forces between the ball and the bat is correct? Part B: Which statement BEST supports the answer to Part A?

optionsA.A: The force of the ball on the bat was less than the force of the bat on the ball.
optionsA.B: The force of the ball on the bat was equal to the force of the bat on the ball.
optionsA.C: The force of the ball on the bat was greater than the force of the bat on the ball.

optionsB.A: Whenever two objects interact, the more massive object always applies a greater force than the less massive object.
optionsB.B: Whenever two objects interact, the faster object always applies a greater force than the slower object.
optionsB.C: Whenever two objects interact, they always apply equal and opposite forces on each other.
optionsB.D: Whenever two objects interact, their forces always combine and are applied in the direction of the object that is moving the fastest.

items.reasoning: Newton's Third Law: forces are always equal and opposite regardless of mass or speed.

items.prompt: A student sets a 0.4 kilogram (kg) soccer ball on the ground and gives it a hard kick. The ball traveled a distance of 37 meters (m). The acceleration of the ball was 2,550 meters per second squared (m/s2). Based on the data, how much force in newtons (N) did the student apply to the ball?
items.reasoning: F=ma=0.4*2550=1020N. The 37m distance is a distractor/irrelevant value (not needed for this calculation).

items.prompt: [REWRITE TARGET - originally select-TWO] A researcher observes a car speeding up from rest: mass 1,000 kg, speed increased for 7 seconds, started from rest, acceleration was 4 m/s2, traveled a total of 300 m. Which two data points, together, are needed to calculate the net force acting on the car?

options.A: Mass and acceleration
options.B: Mass and total distance traveled
options.C: Time elapsed and total distance traveled
options.D: Starting speed and time elapsed

items.reasoning: Net force = mass x acceleration (F=ma); distance and time are not needed if acceleration is already given directly. Converted from a 'select TWO from five' original format into a single 4-option MC per pipeline rewrite step.

items.prompt: A student creates a dichotomous key for shark orders. Step 1: flat body->Squatiniformes, else go to 2. Step 2: long saw-like snout->Pristiophoriformes, else go to 3. Step 3: wide T-shaped head->Carcharhiniformes, else go to 4. Step 4: one large fin on back->Lamniformes; multiple large fins on back->Heterodontiformes. A shark has a long, round body (not flat), a pointed (not saw-like) snout, no wide T-shaped head, and one large dorsal fin. Which order does it belong to?

options.A: Pristiophoriformes
options.B: Carcharhiniformes
options.C: Lamniformes
options.D: Heterodontiformes

items.reasoning: Tracing the key: round body (not flat, skip 1a) -> not saw-like snout (skip 2a) -> not T-shaped head (skip 3a) -> one large fin (4a) = Lamniformes.

items.prompt: A scientist studies hydras, which reproduce by budding: a piece of the adult hydra breaks off and becomes a separate organism. Which statement accurately describes the parent hydra?

options.A: The parent hydra used asexual reproduction and is genetically identical to the newly formed hydra.
options.B: The parent hydra used sexual reproduction and is genetically identical to the newly formed hydra.
options.C: The parent hydra used asexual reproduction and is genetically different from the newly formed hydra.
options.D: The parent hydra used sexual reproduction and is genetically different from the newly formed hydra.

items.reasoning: Budding is asexual reproduction (one parent, no gamete fusion), producing a genetically identical clone.

items.prompt: [REWRITE TARGET - restated from graph] A car drives down a long road. Over a 14-minute trip, the car traveled a total distance of 12 km (with some stops along the way). What was the car's average speed in kilometers per minute for the entire trip?

options.A: 12 km/min
options.B: 0.86 km/min
options.C: 0.23 km/min
options.D: 1.17 km/min

items.reasoning: Average speed = total distance / total time = 12km / 14min = 0.857 km/min, matching option B. Restated the total distance/time directly from the source graph's endpoints (12km at 14min) rather than the full multi-segment plot, since only the total average is asked.

items.prompt: Satellite images show how the Padma River in Bangladesh has changed shape between 1988, 1998, and 2018. Which of these MOST LIKELY caused the changes in the shape of the river?

options.A: The weathering of sediment within the river caused landslides along the riverbank.
options.B: Increased droughts caused weathering and erosion in areas surrounding the river.
options.C: The flow of the water in the river caused erosion along the riverbanks.
options.D: Decreased city development along the riverbanks caused an accumulation of sediment.

items.reasoning: Rivers naturally change shape over decades primarily through erosion caused by flowing water along their banks - the most direct, well-established cause, versus the more speculative/incorrect distractors.

items.prompt: A student examines a cell under a microscope and identifies two features: a large vacuole and a cell wall. Which table correctly describes the cell type and the functions of these two features?

options.A: Plant cell; cell wall regulates transport of materials; vacuole is site of photosynthesis
options.B: Animal cell; cell wall is site of cellular respiration; vacuole directs operations within the cell
options.C: Plant cell; cell wall provides structure for the cell; vacuole stores and transports molecules
options.D: Animal cell; cell wall directs operations within the cell; vacuole provides a site for chemical reactions

items.reasoning: A cell wall indicates a plant cell (animal cells lack cell walls). The cell wall's true function is structural support; the vacuole's true function is storage/transport of molecules and water - matching option C exactly. The other options misattribute cell type or invent incorrect organelle functions (chloroplasts do photosynthesis, not vacuoles; mitochondria do respiration, not cell walls; nucleus directs cell activities, not cell wall).

items.prompt: A student turns on a battery-operated fan (batteries in the base). After five minutes, the base of the fan is warm. Which statement BEST describes the conversion of energy taking place in the fan?

options.A: Chemical energy is being converted into mechanical energy and light energy.
options.B: Chemical energy is being converted into mechanical energy and thermal energy.
options.C: Electrical energy is being converted into chemical energy and light energy.
options.D: Electrical energy is being converted into thermal energy and sound energy.

items.reasoning: Batteries store chemical potential energy, converted by the motor mostly into mechanical energy (spinning blades) with some lost as thermal energy (the warmth noticed) - no light is produced by a fan, and batteries do not receive electrical energy (they supply it), ruling out C and D.

items.prompt: A student wants to plan a family camping trip during a full moon. The moon is currently in its first quarter phase. About how many days does the student need to wait to go camping on the night of a full moon?

options.A: 4 days
options.B: 8 days
options.C: 13 days
options.D: 20 days

items.reasoning: The lunar cycle is about 29.5 days; first quarter to full moon is about one-quarter cycle later, roughly 7-8 days.

items.prompt: Which environmental change would MOST LIKELY have long-term effects on both the environment and the species within the environment?

options.A: High amounts of rainfall that cause flood conditions for three months
options.B: Clearing out sections of rain forest, degrading soil quality in a specific region
options.C: A large amount of pests that destroy a season's crops
options.D: A planned burn, resulting in the loss of some trees

items.reasoning: Deforestation with soil degradation is a lasting, difficult-to-reverse change, unlike the other options which are temporary/seasonal/limited-scope events.

items.prompt: Table of material characteristics: X (solid, shiny, brittle, conducts thermal energy), Y (solid, shiny, malleable, conducts electricity), Z (solid, dull, brittle, poor conductor of electricity). How could the materials BEST be classified?

options.A: X: Metal, Y: Metalloid, Z: Nonmetal
options.B: X: Nonmetal, Y: Metal, Z: Nonmetal
options.C: X: Metalloid, Y: Metalloid, Z: Nonmetal
options.D: X: Metalloid, Y: Metal, Z: Nonmetal

items.reasoning: X is shiny and conducts thermal energy but is brittle (not malleable) - a metalloid trait mix; Y is shiny, malleable, conducts electricity - classic metal; Z is dull, brittle, poor conductor - classic nonmetal. Note: I flag this one for extra reviewer scrutiny since X's exact classification (metalloid vs metal) is genuinely borderline/ambiguous from the traits given and worth double-checking, more than the other items.

items.prompt: A student drinks a beverage that contains 78 grams of sugar. Which system produces the hormone insulin that helps break down the sugar in the human body?

options.A: Endocrine system
options.B: Excretory system
options.C: Integumentary system
options.D: Circulatory system

items.reasoning: Insulin is produced by the pancreas, part of the endocrine system.

items.prompt: Scientists have found some of the same types of rock containing the same types of fossil species in Africa and Antarctica. Which explanation does this information support?

options.A: Both continents gradually increased in size over time.
options.B: Both continents were attached by glacial ice millions of years ago.
options.C: Both continents were attached but drifted away from each other over time.
options.D: Both continents were underwater millions of years ago.

items.reasoning: Matching rock/fossil evidence across now-separated continents is classic evidence for continental drift/plate tectonics - the continents were once joined (e.g., Gondwana) and drifted apart.
